column2: Authoritative route ownership: which catalog section describes the screen a
Route ownership used to be inferred from the `route` column of individual
family rows in status.<section>.tsv. That column is per-family detail
("/ -> openModal('bridge')"), not a section-level claim, and inferring
ownership from it produced two wrong answers:
1. FOUR sections appeared to claim "/" — home, onboarding, trade, wallet —
leaving 162 bugs unattributable. The reason is that "/" is not one route.
It is the root of THREE DIFFERENT DEPLOYED APPS:
onboarding-> the skai-landing root        (marked "(skai-landing)" in its route cells)
A bug url from skai.trade "/" belongs to exactly one of those. Without an
app column there is no way to say which.
2. /launchpad (56 bugs) and /sports (37) appeared to be claimed by NOBODY,
because no family row happened to name them — even though both surfaces
app = which deployed surface the route lives on. Bug reports carry a url from
the main app, so only app=main rows are eligible to match them.
EVIDENCE for the two routes that had no owner:
/sports   -> play.   All 15 sampled node-ids from the 37 /sports bugs are in
play.nodes.txt. The sportsbook screens sit on the ✅ Play page.
/launchpad-> trade-2. 42 of the 56 bugs point at Skai-Web-App-2 nodes
"Skai > Launch > create token" and "Skai > Launch > Live" on the
✅ Trade 2 page. The other 14 point at Skai-Web-App file-1 nodes
a residual gap, recorded rather than papered over.
⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-19: /play/keno and /play/towers were listed here as
live routes. Neither exists in src/App.tsx. Verified by enumerating every
route in that file: the ONLY games with a routed page are blackjack,
chicken, coinflip, crash, darts, dice, hilo, mines, plinko and scratchers
— exactly the ten that have a *PageSections.tsx. Keno, towers, rps,
fortune-wheel, roulette, baccarat, bingo, video-poker, limbo and slide are
MODAL-ONLY: reachable from the Play hub, with no URL of their own.
The rows are kept below, commented, because the sections are real and a
route may still be wanted — they were just never wired.
